findings.summary: A legitimate re-park after an acknowledged resume has no path forward: the coordinator returns blocked+waiting_on=decision while acknowledging message_id, so N7 correctly does not reject, after_coordinator routes back to decision_interrupt on the same round_no, ask() re-finds the same checkpoint_for_round question, and the resume_key is therefore identical to the one whose resume receipt was already consumed -- GoalInterruptBridge then reports skipped:already_resumed forever. Outside the spec's enumerated behaviors (item 4 covers only the unacknowledged repeat of the same prior_terminal), so it does not block approval, but a genuinely new decision wait inside a resumed round cannot be answered.

resolve_decision unions every question note _question_texts scanned (up to MAX_QUESTION_SCAN_PAGES * board_page_limit = 10000 notes) into candidate_ids, and _referenced_questions issues one refs_to HTTP call per candidate for every decision processed -- an O(board size) request fan-out per decision, where the pre-change path only queried the waiting owners' own question ids.

A wake fact arriving during a suspension (inbox message or goal.md revision change) relaunches the line, which re-enters decision_interrupt and rewrites terminal.json under a fresh uuid run_id; park_state then re-establishes and _ask_board publishes a second question note under parked:<folder>:<new_run_id>, while the interrupt still tracks the original note. A human answering the newer note wakes the parked line rather than resuming the interrupt.

No test asserts that build_line actually populates deps.interrupt -- the exact wiring whose absence was attempt 1's blocker. tests/test_line_restart.py and tests/test_envelope_facts.py call build_line but only inspect thread_id and prior_terminal, and every E2 graph test constructs LineDeps by hand, so a regression that drops the interrupt= argument would leave the whole suite green.

newest_decision, compensate_decision and decision_is_newer have no production callers: GoalInterruptBridge._decision_chain sorts inline and the forward-monotonic check lives in GoalInterruptStore.record_compensation. Spec item 7's selection rule is genuinely implemented, but these three exported helpers are exercised only by tests.

Two verification facts recorded rather than asserted. This reviewer has file inspection only and no shell, so the prescribed `git diff --exit-code b572ca66 2886376b -- . ':(exclude).dev-dispatch'` was not executed and tree equality between the two SHAs is unverified; the .dev-dispatch/ namespace as inspected holds only metadata (development.json, run-config.json, spec, handoffs, reviews, feedback index) and no product file carries review-stage content, consistent with a compliant metadata-only materialization. Separately, the committed implement handoff records work_head_commit 6420ea4c3c034dc73bf0b1bd9f394dfee7bf3f83 while the dispatch context names b572ca66d173c138eaa56b5dd60fa1d9cdc42b9f as the product commit -- the same mismatch shape all three prior final reviews recorded.
